title: What superintelligence actually means — and why today's AI isn't it

chapters.headline: A term is being spent on tools that don't match it
points: An executive order proclaims the dawn of an era of "Super Intelligence"; the term is being applied to today's AI models
Sandra Rogers, PhD, argues this is a category error worth correcting before it hardens into habit
When the words are wrong, budgets, timelines, training plans, and safety rules inherit the error
chapters.takeaway: Vocabulary is a foundational assumption — get it wrong and everything built on it inherits the error.

chapters.headline: Three words, three different things
points: Narrow AI is everything that actually exists today: chatbots, image generators, recommendation engines, agentic assistants
AGI — human-level intellect across domains — is a theoretical milestone. It does not exist
Superintelligence would exceed the best human minds in practically every field. It does not exist either
chapters.takeaway: Every tool we deploy, teach, or evaluate sits on the first rung. All of it.

chapters.headline: Buying and planning against a capability that isn't there
points: Buying: a pitch deck that says "superintelligence" sells a capability that does not exist — a term is not evidence
Planning: a training program for narrow AI looks nothing like one designed for a hypothetical general intelligence
Plan for science fiction and you misallocate real money, real curriculum, and real people's time
chapters.takeaway: Confident wording does not mean the claim is right.

chapters.headline: Oversight fits the category of the thing governed
points: A narrow tool needs what we already know how to do: access controls, verification, a human accountable for the output
Blurring the category cuts both ways — fearing the tool you actually have, and under-preparing for systems that don't exist yet
Precision is what keeps both errors out
chapters.takeaway: Governance fits the category of the thing governed.

chapters.headline: Fixed terms, and one question to steal
points: Our website and AI 101 course materials now teach the ladder explicitly; the terms are fixed
"AI" stays for today's real technology; "SI" is used only for the third rung, the theoretical category
The course keeps its name: AI 101 teaches what AI is — and now, on the record, what AI is not
chapters.takeaway: The next time a pitch says superintelligence, ask: which rung? If the speaker can't answer, you have learned something about the pitch.
